name: Moebius Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Facial Palsy with Abducens Nerve Palsy

criteria.description: Congenital, non-progressive facial paralysis involving the seventh cranial nerve
Congenital abducens nerve (sixth cranial nerve) palsy causing impaired lateral eye movement
Onset present at birth with no progressive neurological deterioration
Presence of limb abnormalities such as clubfoot or syndactyly
Involvement of additional cranial nerves (e.g., hypoglossal, trigeminal)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital facial paralysis and abducens nerve palsy with onset at birth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to facial weakness and inability to smile or close eyes fully

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abducens nerve (VI) palsy causing lateral gaze palsy
pathognomonic.notes: Results in impaired horizontal eye movement
Symptoms present at birth and non-progressive

common.notes: Due to cranial nerve involvement affecting swallowing

common.symptomName: Speech impairment due to facial and tongue weakness
Limb malformations such as clubfoot or syndactyly

common.notes: Due to inability to close eyelids fully

common.symptomName: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) palsy causing tongue weakness
common.notes: May contribute to feeding and speech difficulties

occasional.notes: Due to cranial nerve dysfunction affecting airway protection
Possible due to cranial nerve involvement

rare.notes: Not typical but reported in some cases
Rare and not a primary feature

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; used to exclude other conditions
imaging: MRI may show hypoplasia or absence of facial and abducens cranial nerve nuclei
genetic: Mutations in PLXND1 and REV3L genes reported in some cases
Mostly sporadic with rare familial cases
other: Electromyography shows denervation of facial muscles
Clinical diagnosis based on cranial nerve palsies

distinguishingFeatures: Limited horizontal eye movement due to abducens nerve absence

redFlags: Inability to close eyelids leading to corneal ulceration
Severe feeding difficulties causing failure to thrive
references: Verzijl HT, van der Zwaag B, Cruysberg JR, et al. Clinical and genetic aspects of Moebius syndrome: an update. Eur J Med Genet. 2010;53(4):186-193.
Briegel W. Moebius sequence: a review. Clin Genet. 2006;70(4):283-291.
Bavinck JN, Weaver DD. Transient hypoxic damage to the brainstem as a cause of Moebius syndrome. Am J Med Genet. 1986;25(1):99-112.
